target: Mohon doa restu untuk pernikahan putra kami bulan depan.
english: We ask for your blessing for our son's wedding next month.
tip: doa restu = 'prayers and blessing' — a fixed wedding-invitation phrase.

target: Atas kehadiran dan doa Bapak Ibu, kami ucapkan terima kasih.
english: For your presence and prayers, we express our thanks.
tip: Invitation closer: atas kehadiran ... terima kasih — thanks given before the event happens.

target: Kami mohon kehadiran Bapak tepat waktu karena acara dimulai sore hari.
english: We request your presence on time because the event begins in the late afternoon.
tip: mohon kehadiran = 'we request your presence' — spoken this is just: datang ya.

target: Turut mengundang keluarga besar Wijaya dan rekan kantor.
english: Also extending the invitation: the extended Wijaya family and office colleagues.
tip: Turut mengundang = 'also inviting' — the line listing extra hosts at the bottom of invitations.

target: Kehadiran Bapak dan Ibu akan menjadi kehormatan bagi keluarga kami.
english: Your presence will be an honor for our family.
tip: bagi = formal 'untuk' (for) — invitation and news word; spoken: untuk keluarga kami.

target: Kami mengundang seluruh warga untuk mengikuti kerja bakti hari Minggu pagi.
english: We invite all residents to join the community work day on Sunday morning.
tip: kerja bakti = 'community work day' — a fixed term on neighborhood invitations.

target: Mohon kehadiran Ibu pada pertemuan orang tua murid hari Sabtu.
english: We request your presence, Madam, at the parents' meeting on Saturday.
tip: pertemuan = formal 'meeting', from bertemu — schools write pertemuan, parents say rapat.

target: Undangan ini berlaku untuk dua orang termasuk anak-anak.
english: This invitation is valid for two people, including children.
tip: Termasuk is literally 'entered (into the group)' – masuk with ter-. Termasuk anak-anak means the children are counted in: 'including'.

target: Besar harapan kami Bapak dapat hadir dan memberikan sambutan.
english: It is our great hope that you can attend and give a speech.
tip: Besar harapan kami = 'it is our great hope' — a super-polite invitation formula.

target: Kami menantikan kehadiran Anda sekeluarga pada acara ulang tahun perusahaan.
english: We look forward to the presence of you and your family at the company anniversary event.
tip: menantikan = 'to look forward to, await' — the formal menunggu; invitations love it.

target: Nasabah dimohon mengambil nomor antrean sebelum menuju loket.
english: Customers are requested to take a queue number before proceeding to the counter.
tip: nasabah = 'bank customer' — only banks use it; shops say pelanggan or pembeli.

target: Biaya administrasi sebesar lima ribu rupiah dikenakan untuk setiap transaksi.
english: An administration fee of five thousand rupiah is charged for each transaction.
tip: sebesar = 'in the amount of' (se- + besar) — money notices use it before every figure.

target: Mesin ATM di lantai satu sedang dalam perbaikan sementara.
english: The ATM on the first floor is temporarily under repair.
tip: sedang dalam perbaikan = 'under repair', notice formula — spoken: lagi diperbaiki.

target: Mohon jangan memberikan kata sandi Anda kepada siapa pun.
english: Please do not give your password to anyone.
tip: kata sandi = official 'password' — most Indonesians just say password; sandi = code.

target: Layanan pelanggan kami dapat dihubungi dua puluh empat jam.
english: Our customer service can be reached twenty-four hours a day.
tip: layanan = formal 'service', from melayani — in speech, customer service is just CS (ce-es).

target: Rapat seluruh karyawan akan diadakan hari Jumat pukul dua siang.
english: An all-staff meeting will be held on Friday at two in the afternoon.
tip: karyawan = 'employee', the office word — casual speech says pegawai or orang kantor.

target: Seluruh karyawan diwajibkan mengikuti pelatihan keselamatan kerja bulan depan.
english: All employees are required to attend the occupational safety training next month.
tip: diwajibkan = 'are required to', HR passive — spoken: semua harus ikut.

target: Kartu yang tertelan mesin dapat diambil di kantor cabang terdekat.
english: A card swallowed by the machine can be collected at the nearest branch office.
tip: tertelan = 'accidentally swallowed' — ter- marks accidents: kartunya tertelan mesin.

target: Penarikan uang di atas sepuluh juta harap dikonfirmasi sehari sebelumnya.
english: Withdrawals above ten million should be confirmed one day in advance.
tip: penarikan uang = 'withdrawal', bank language — spoken: mau ambil uang.

target: Sistem kami akan diperbarui malam ini mulai pukul sebelas.
english: Our system will be updated tonight starting at eleven.
tip: diperbarui = 'be updated, renewed', from baru (new) — memper- means 'make more X'.

target: Selama jam istirahat, pelayanan di loket dua dihentikan sementara.
english: During the break, service at counter two is temporarily suspended.
tip: dihentikan sementara = 'temporarily suspended', notice-speak — spoken: loketnya tutup dulu.

target: Mohon maaf, layanan transfer antarbank sedang mengalami gangguan.
english: We apologize; the interbank transfer service is currently experiencing a disruption.
tip: mengalami gangguan = 'experiencing a disruption', outage-notice formula — spoken: lagi error.

target: Terima kasih atas kepercayaan Anda kepada bank kami selama ini.
english: Thank you for your trust in our bank all this time.
tip: atas after terima kasih = formal 'for': terima kasih atas kepercayaan Anda — speech drops atas.

target: Aku nggak bisa datang ke acara kantor besok malam.
english: I can't make it to the office event tomorrow night.
tip: Heard everywhere in speech: nggak = tidak. Nggak bisa = tidak bisa (can't). In writing, use tidak.

target: Mereka nggak jadi pindah ke Surabaya karena anaknya betah di sini.
english: They ended up not moving to Surabaya because their kid feels at home here.
tip: Nggak jadi = 'ended up not happening': jadi means 'materialize', so nggak jadi pindah says the move was planned and then fell through.

target: Nggak apa-apa, besok kita coba lagi dari awal.
english: It's okay, tomorrow we'll try again from the start.
tip: Nggak apa-apa = tidak apa-apa ('it's okay') — one of the most common spoken phrases.

target: Kamu udah makan belum? Aku baru mau pesan nasi goreng.
english: Have you eaten yet? I was just about to order fried rice.
tip: Udah = sudah in speech: udah makan? = sudah makan? (eaten yet?)

target: Dia udah berangkat ke bandara sejak jam lima pagi.
english: She already left for the airport at five in the morning.
tip: Udah berangkat = sudah berangkat (already left). Spoken form; write sudah.

target: Duduk di sini aja, dekat jendela biar adem.
english: Just sit here, near the window so it's cooler.
tip: Aja = saja (just): di sini aja = di sini saja (just here).

target: Kamu tanya aja langsung ke petugas di loket dua.
english: Just go ask the officer at counter two directly.
tip: Tanya aja = tanya saja ('just ask'). Aja follows the word it limits.
